audit.primary_source_citation: PRIMARY (first to establish the claim as stated): Keskin DB, Allan DSJ, Rybalov B, Andzelm MM, Stern JNH, Kopcow HD, Koopman LA, Strominger JL. "TGFbeta promotes conversion of CD16+ peripheral blood NK cells into CD16- NK cells with similarities to decidual NK cells." Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2007;104(9):3378-83. PMID 17360654; PMC1805591; doi:10.1073/pnas.0611098104. CONFIRMATORY/EXTENSION (not primary): Cerdeira AS, Rajakumar A, Royle CM, Lo A, Husain Z, Thadhani RI, Sukhatme VP, Karumanchi SA, Kopcow HD. "Conversion of peripheral blood NK cells to a decidual NK-like phenotype by a cocktail of defined factors." J Immunol 2013;190(8):3939-48. PMID 23487420; PMC3742368; doi:10.4049/jimmunol.1202582. Both hint papers were located and read in full; neither is a review. Note the hint "Keskin 2007 = TGF-beta1 + IL-15" is only half right: IL-15 AND SCF (20 ng/ml each) were in EVERY arm including the control, so the paper's contrast is TGF-beta1 (or decidual stromal conditioned medium) on top of a constant IL-15/SCF background, not "TGF-beta1 + IL-15 vs nothing".

NB: the repo helper `lit.py methods` returned STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY for both PMC1805591 and PMC3742368 - that is a bug/limitation of the helper's PMC path, not an availability problem; both full texts were retrievable by direct curl of pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and are now archived under refs/. PARTIAL/UNOBTAINABLE elsewhere: Strunz 2021 Sci Immunol (PMID 33617461) - science.org returned HTTP 403, no PMC deposit; its uterus-transplant chimerism methods (n patients, timepoints, HLA/SNP genotyping detail) were NOT read and are recorded from abstract only. Strunz/Ivarsson Sci Transl Med 2026 (PMID 41811987, doi 10.1126/scitranslmed.adp2583) - paywalled, methods NOT read; a bioRxiv preprint exists (10.1101/2024.03.04.583277) but was not fetched. Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026 (PMID 42417504) methods were read via WebFetch of elifesciences.org, not archived to refs/.
audit.species: Human (Keskin 2007 and Cerdeira 2013: human peripheral blood NK from healthy donors / discarded leukopacks; human first-trimester decidua, 6-12 weeks gestation, elective terminations). The only IN VIVO evidence bearing on this claim is in a different species (mouse: Chantakru 2002; Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026) or in human transplant recipients (Strunz 2021; Strunz 2026) - see counter_evidence and audit_overturns_detail.
audit.what_was_measured: In human, peripheral-blood NK cells negatively enriched with RosetteSep from healthy donors (and, in the key experiments, FACS-sorted into CD56+CD16+ and CD56+CD16- fractions that were CD9-negative and CD103-negative at day 0) were cultured in vitro for 2-3 weeks at 1e6 cells/ml in Myelocult + 10% human serum + 5% FCS with a constant background of 20 ng/ml IL-15 + 20 ng/ml SCF, either alone (control), or with 2 or 10 ng/ml recombinant TGF-beta1, or in conditioned medium from cultured first-trimester decidual stromal cells; at the 2-3 week endpoint the readout was surface staining by flow cytometry for CD56, CD16, CD9, CD103 (alphaE integrin) and pooled anti-KIR mAb (HP3-E4 + CH-L + DX9), scored as percentage of cells in each gate, in 15-16 independent donor cultures. Supporting arms: TGF-beta1 protein in decidual stromal conditioned medium by ELISA (81-419 pg/ml) across 17 CM preparations; blockade with pan-TGF-beta1/2/3 mAb 1D11 vs isotype; and, separately, decidual Lin-CD34+CD45+ cells sorted from decidua (250-500 cells/well) cultured ~30 days in the same CM + IL-15 + SCF and scored for CD56/CD16/CD9/CD94 in 4 experiments. In Cerdeira 2013 the analogous readout was, in human, pNK cultured 7 days at 1% O2 vs 21% O2 with 10 ng/ml IL-15 +/- 2 ng/ml TGF-beta1 +/- 1 uM 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine, with day-7 flow cytometry for CD9/CD49a/KIR/chemokine receptors gated separately on CD56bright-CD16- and CD56dim-CD16+ events, VEGF-A ELISA, 4h 51Cr release on K562, HUVEC tube formation, and HTR-8/SVneo Matrigel invasion (n=10 blood donors for the invasion endpoint). No timepoint in either paper is an in vivo timepoint; no decidua was ever entered by a labelled blood NK cell in either paper.
audit.n: Keskin 2007 (primary): 16 independent pNK cultures for the CD56+CD16- shift with decidual stromal CM (effect seen in 12/16, paired t-test p=0.002, SI Table 1); 15 independent experiments for the KIR readout; 17 CM preparations for the TGF-beta1 ELISA (and n=7 and n=8 for the +/- MPA/estradiol ELISA arms); 4 experiments for decidual Lin-CD34+CD45+ progenitor differentiation (dNK-like output in 3/4). The number of distinct blood donors and the number of distinct decidua donors are NEVER stated anywhere in the paper - "independent experiments" is the only unit reported, and each figure panel is labelled "representative". Cerdeira 2013: CD9 induction "representative of 10 experiments" (effect in 7/10 for the hypoxia-enhanced MFI), KIR "representative of 5 experiments"; VEGF-A n=3-4 experiments; HUVEC tube formation n=6; cytotoxicity n=2-3; trophoblast invasion N=10 donors (the only place a donor count is given); dNK IL-8 n=4 samples. Comparator in vivo work (not the primary source): Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026 adoptive transfer n=4 pregnant dams, conditional-knockout arm n=5 TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta vs n=6 littermate controls.
audit.n_unit: independent in vitro experiments / cultures (Keskin: one blood-donor NK preparation + one decidua-derived conditioned-medium preparation per experiment). NOT donors - donor counts are unreported in the primary source. NOT cells. The only true donor-unit n anywhere in the two human papers is Cerdeira's N=10 blood donors for the trophoblast-invasion functional endpoint. For the mouse in vivo comparator the unit is dams (n=4 transfer; n=5 vs 6 knockout), with 9-54 implantation sites per group as a sub-unit.
audit.controls: Keskin 2007 - PRESENT: paired same-donor medium-only arm (IL-15 + SCF, no TGF-beta1/no CM) run alongside every treated culture, with paired t-test; day-0 baseline staining establishing that input cells were CD9-negative, CD103-negative and only ~3% CD16-negative; isotype-control mAb histograms for CD9, CD103 and KIR; post-sort purity plots for the CD16+ vs CD16- fractions (Fig 5C); a genuine specificity control in the form of pan-TGF-beta1/2/3 neutralising mAb 1D11 (10 ug/ml) vs isotype pre-treatment of the conditioned medium, which abolished both the CD16 loss and the CD9 gain; decidual stromal preparations verified CD14-negative and CD45-negative before CM harvest; sorted KIR- pNK tested and shown NOT to acquire KIR (data not shown). ABSENT AND DECISIVE: no proliferation/division tracking (no CFSE, no Ki67, no cell counts per gate), so a gain in the PERCENTAGE of CD16-CD9+ cells cannot be separated from differential proliferation or differential death; no clonal barcoding, no genetic lineage tracing, no live imaging of a single cell losing CD16 and gaining CD9; no rigorous quantification of post-sort CD16- contamination in the critical CD16+ sorted arm; no in vivo arm of any kind. Cerdeira 2013 - PRESENT: paired same-donor 21% O2 control for every 1% O2 culture, Aza and TGF-beta1 dose-response, isotype controls, FACS-sorted 99%-pure CD56bright-CD16- and CD56dim-CD16+ subsets for the VEGF-A endpoint, HIF-1alpha immunoblot as a hypoxia-exposure control, and a striking reverse control (ex vivo dNK cells lose KIR and regain K562 cytotoxicity within 7-10 days of culture). ABSENT: the central phenotype experiments start from BULK enriched pNK, not from sorted CD56dim-CD16+ cells, and are then gated on the CD56bright-CD16- fraction - so the "converted" cells are read out inside a gate that the paper's own Fig 2a-2b shows is ENRICHED by the treatment; again no division tracking or barcoding.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET IS SELECTED / DIFFERENTIALLY EXPANDED, NOT CONVERTED - and the primary source itself supplies the ammunition. Keskin's own control arm states that IL-15 + SCF alone already increases the CD56+CD16- percentage, and the authors attribute this to "a greater proliferation of CD16- pNK cells, which are known to respond to these cytokines with greater proliferation, compared with CD16+ pNK cells". Over 2-3 weeks in IL-15/SCF, a 1-2% CD16- contaminant surviving the CD16+ sort needs only a modest proliferative advantage to dominate the well; TGF-beta1 is independently anti-proliferative for CD56dim NK, which would widen that advantage without any cell changing identity. Because the readout is percentage-in-gate by flow cytometry with no CFSE, no absolute counts, no Ki67 and no barcode, the assay is formally incapable of distinguishing conversion from selective outgrowth. Cerdeira 2013 makes this explicit in its own words for its own system - "Cultures under hypoxia were enriched in CD56Bright CD16- NK cells relative to cultures under 21% O2" and "hypoxia ... enriches pNK cell cultures in CD56Bright CD16- cells" - and then reads CD9/KIR out inside that enriched gate, starting from bulk pNK rather than sorted CD56dim cells. SECOND ALTERNATIVE - the endpoint markers are a generic TGF-beta / tissue-residency imprint, not decidual identity: CD9, CD103 and CD49a are TGF-beta-induced on NK cells in any tissue, and Keskin concedes in the Discussion that "the changes observed may not be specific to the decidual tissue but may occur when NK cells enter any tissue expressing TGF-beta"; CD9 is also inducible by IL-2/PHA. So "dNK-like" may name a cytokine signature, not a lineage destination. THIRD - TWO INDEPENDENT ORIGINS, again from inside the primary source: Keskin Fig 6 shows decidual Lin-CD34+CD45+ HPC generating CD56superbright CD16- CD9+ CD94+ cells in 3/4 experiments, i.e. the same paper offers a local-precursor route that does not pass through pbNK at all, and the authors' own summary is that "CD16+ pNK cells or decidual HPC, or both, are possible precursors". FOURTH - CULTURE ARTEFACT with demonstrated bidirectionality: Cerdeira Fig 1 shows ex vivo dNK cells LOSING KIR and REGAINING cytotoxicity within 7-10 days of the same IL-15 medium, so these markers are labile culture readouts that move in whichever direction the medium pushes; a marker that reverses in a week is weak evidence of a lineage transition.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, on both sides. AGAINST the pbNK-origin claim (local / pre-existing precursor): (1) Vacca P et al., PNAS 2011;108(6):2402-7, PMID 21248224 - CD34+ hematopoietic precursors are present in human decidua, differ from cord- and peripheral-blood CD34+ cells, are already NK-committed (CD122+ CD127+, E4BP4/ID2 mRNA), and differentiate into CD56bright CD16- KIR+/- IL-8/IL-22-producing NK cells upon coculture with decidual stromal cells - a local origin bypassing pbNK entirely. (2) Male V, Hughes T, McClory S, Colucci F, Caligiuri MA, Moffett A, J Immunol 2010;185:3913-18, PMID 20802153 - stage-3 CD34-CD117+CD94- NK precursors are resident in human uterine mucosa and give rise to stage-4-like cells in vitro; the authors propose recruitment of an IMMATURE precursor, not of a mature pbNK. (3) Keskin 2007's own Fig 6: decidual Lin-CD34+CD45+ HPC generate CD56superbright CD16- CD9+ CD94+ cells in 3/4 experiments. (4) Cerdeira 2013's own Fig 2a-2b hypoxia-enrichment of a pre-existing CD56bright CD16- subset. (5) Strunz B et al., Sci Immunol 2021;6:eabb7800, PMID 33617461 (abstract only; science.org 403) - a CONTINUOUS in-situ uNK differentiation pathway driven by IL-15 with sequential KIR then CD39 acquisition, coupled to endometrial regeneration: the decidual phenotype as the end of a local maturation series rather than a direct pbNK conversion. FOR the claim / against the local-only alternative: (6) Chantakru S et al., J Immunol 2002;168:22-8, PMID 11751942 - in mouse, orthotopic uterine grafts from NK-competent donors into NK/uNK-deficient recipients did NOT generate uNK cells (pre-uNK do not self-renew in uterus), while grafting spleen/lymph-node cells from pregnant donors into mated NK-deficient recipients DID reconstitute uNK; genuine in vivo transfer, but the transferred entity is a secondary-lymphoid-tissue precursor, not a mature pbNK. (7) Strunz 2021 and Strunz B, Ivarsson MA, Sun D et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 41811987 (abstract/press only; paywalled) - uterus-transplant recipients' uNK carry the RECIPIENT genotype, and after HSCT the endometrial immune compartment including tissue-resident lymphocytes is DONOR-derived (one case male-origin), by SNP/HLA-disparity single-cell genotyping: blood-borne replenishment of the human uterine NK niche in vivo, but consistent with a haematopoietic precursor rather than a mature pbNK. (8) Barahona JD, Yang L, Nelson DM, Yokoyama WM, eLife 2026;15:RP109878, PMID 42417504 - mouse in vivo OBS_TRANSFER + OBS_GENETIC, detailed in audit_overturns_detail.
audit.downstream_dependency: Concrete, named, inside this screen's own registry (/home/user/aaa/phaseA/claims.json): claim X3 ("Tumour NK -> decidual-like / pro-angiogenic phenotype", currently logged "INFERENCE (phenotypic similarity)") and claim T5 ("Glycodelin-A -> dNK-like phenotype", currently logged "IN VITRO") both inherit their ENTIRE operational definition of the "dNK-like" endpoint - CD16-/CD9+/CD49a+/KIR+/VEGF-secreting/hypocytotoxic - from the Keskin-Cerdeira in vitro induction protocol. If that endpoint is a generic TGF-beta/hypoxia imprint rather than decidual identity (the second alternative above), X3 and T5 lose the thing they are measuring against, and their gradings must degrade to INF_MARKER on a non-specific marker set. Claim T1 ("cNK -> trNK") and T2 ("cNK -> uterine trNK") are adjacent: T2's mouse OBS_TRANSFER result is routinely read back onto T3 as if it validated the human claim, which this audit shows it does not (different species, different endpoint markers). Outside the registry, the concrete named dependency is Kopcow HD / Cerdeira AS et al., PLoS One 2016;11:e0164353, PMID 27736914, "Induced Human Decidual NK-Like Cells Improve Utero-Placental Perfusion in Mice", which manufactures idNK cells by exactly this hypoxia/TGF-beta1/5-aza protocol and infuses them into pregnant immunocompromised mice as a proposed preeclampsia cell therapy - a translational program resting on the assumption that the in vitro product is a dNK cell.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: CONFIRMED half: for the claim as literally stated in human, "IN VITRO ONLY" is correct. Both hint papers were located, both are primary (not reviews), both full texts were read, and neither contains a single in vivo experiment - Keskin 2007 is 2-3 weeks of flow cytometry on cultured blood NK, Cerdeira 2013 is 7 days of the same plus ELISA/51Cr/Matrigel. There is NO study in which a labelled or genotype-marked human blood NK cell was shown to enter decidua and acquire the dNK phenotype. OVERTURNED half - "ONLY" is too strong on two counts, and the initial call misses both. (1) MOUSE IN VIVO TRANSFER + GENETIC EVIDENCE NOW EXISTS: Barahona JD, Yang L, Nelson DM, Yokoyama WM, "TGF-beta drives the conversion of conventional NK cells into uterine tissue-resident NK cells to support murine pregnancy", eLife 2026;15:RP109878, PMID 42417504 (bioRxiv preprint PMID 41332720). Methods read from elifesciences.org: 2.5e6 CD45.2+ SPLENIC cNK cells (CD3- CD19- NK1.1+ NKp46+ CD49b+, 87-93% pure) were injected i.v. via tail vein into congenic C57BL/6 CD45.1 pregnant dams at gd0.5 (n=4 dams); by gd10.5 a subset of donor CD45.2+ cells recovered from the gravid uterus had upregulated CD49a and downregulated CD49b, i.e. acquired the CD49a+ CD49b- Eomes+ uterine trNK phenotype, with 3 ug fluorescent anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 given intravascularly 3 min before euthanasia to exclude cells still in the vasculature. Separately, Tgfbr2-floxed x Ncr1-iCre (TGF-betaRII-Ncr1-delta) dams had significantly reduced uterine CD49a+ Eomes+ trNK at gd6.5 (n=5 knockout vs n=6 littermate controls), with rescue by transfer of 3.0e6 CD45.1+ wild-type cNK. That is OBS_TRANSFER plus OBS_GENETIC, in vivo - not INF_INVITRO. Caveats that stop it from simply resolving T3: species is mouse; the endpoint is CD49a+Eomes+ uterine trNK, not the human dNK signature (CD56superbright CD9+ KIR+); and the same registry already logs this as claim T2, so importing it into T3 would double-count. (2) HUMAN IN VIVO GENOTYPE EVIDENCE EXISTS THAT THE UTERINE NK NICHE IS FILLED FROM THE CIRCULATION: Strunz et al. Sci Immunol 2021 (PMID 33617461) report that uNK in uterus-transplant recipients carry the RECIPIENT genotype, and Strunz, Ivarsson, Sun et al. Sci Transl Med 2026 (PMID 41811987) report by single-cell SNP/HLA-disparity genotyping that recipient-derived immune cells replace donor immune cells after uterus transplant while HSCT gives near-complete donor-derived endometrial reconstitution including tissue-resident lymphocytes (one patient reconstituted by male-origin cells). Both are paywalled and their methods were NOT read (science.org 403), so this is recorded as abstract-level only and must not be graded as verified OBS_TRANSFER. Critically, even taken at face value this evidence is compatible with a blood-borne PRECURSOR (HSC / stage-3 NK precursor) rather than with a mature pbNK converting, which is what T3 asserts - and Chantakru 2002, Male 2010 and Vacca 2011 all point to the precursor reading. (3) One further hint correction: the hint's "TGF-beta1 + IL-15" for Keskin understates the culture - IL-15 AND SCF at 20 ng/ml were present in every arm including the control, so the paper never tests TGF-beta1 against a cytokine-free baseline. NET: change the T3 entry from "IN VITRO ONLY (Keskin 2007; Cerdeira 2013)" to "HUMAN EVIDENCE IN VITRO ONLY (INF_INVITRO, percentage-in-gate, no division tracking, selection not excluded); in vivo support is mouse-only (OBS_TRANSFER + OBS_GENETIC, Barahona/Yokoyama 2026 = claim T2) plus unverified human transplant-chimerism data that argue for a blood-borne PRECURSOR rather than mature pbNK conversion."
audit.methods_quote: Keskin 2007, Materials and Methods, "Differentiation of pNK": "NK cells were isolated from peripheral blood of healthy donors by using RosetteSep human NK cell enrichment mixture (Stem Cell Technologies). pNK cells were cultured for 2-3 weeks in 24-well plates (10^6 cells in 1 ml) under the following conditions: (i) normal medium (Myelocult Medium plus 10% human serum, 5% FCS, 20 ng/ml IL-15, and 20 ng/ml SCF), (ii) normal medium additionally supplemented with 2 or 10 ng/ml TGFbeta1, or (iii) decidual stromal CM plus 20 ng/ml IL-15 and 20 ng/ml SCF. ... In certain experiments, pNK cells were separated into CD56+CD16+ and CD56+CD16- populations by flow cytometry sorting before similar culture in vitro." Keskin 2007, Results, the selection-not-conversion admission: "When pNK cells were cultured for 2 weeks in medium supplemented with IL-15 and SCF, the percentage of CD56+CD16- NK cells was increased to some extent. This was likely because of a greater proliferation of CD16- pNK cells, which are known to respond to these cytokines with greater proliferation, compared with CD16+ pNK cells." Keskin 2007, closing sentence of the Discussion: "Thus, CD16+ pNK cells or decidual HPC, or both, are possible precursors of dNK cells. Although it is still not possible to draw conclusions on the nature of the in vivo precursor cells of dNK, this study suggests that TGFbeta may play an important role in influencing the dNK phenotype." Cerdeira 2013, Materials and Methods, "Conversion of pNK cells to dNK-like cells": "Enriched peripheral blood NK cells were seeded at 1x10^6 cells/ml, in IL-15 complete media in the presence or absence of recombinant human TGFbeta1 ... at 2 ng/ml ... and in the presence or absence of Aza ... 1 uM ... One of the NK cell cultures was maintained under 21% O2, the other culture was maintained under hypoxia (1% O2). Cell culture supernatants were harvested after 7 days ..." Cerdeira 2013, Results, its own enrichment statement: "Cultures under hypoxia were enriched in CD56Bright CD16- NK cells relative to cultures under 21% O2."

adv.challenge_reason: LABEL UPHELD (INF_INVITRO), REASONING PARTLY OVERTURNED. I re-pulled the primary source myself. `lit.py methods 17360654 --tag T3` again returned STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T3_PMC1805591.txt), so I re-fetched PMC1805591 directly by curl to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aaa/5f46e874-56b9-5c6b-9d27-d08dbfb1d5d8/scratchpad/keskin_text.txt (43,734 chars) and read the Materials and Methods and Results independently. (1) NO OBS_* CLASS WAS WRONGLY CREDITED. Keskin 2007 is 2-3 wk of 24-well culture (10^6 pNK/ml, Myelocult + 10% human serum + 5% FCS + 20 ng/ml IL-15 + 20 ng/ml SCF in EVERY arm, +/- 2 or 10 ng/ml TGF-beta1 or decidual stromal CM) with surface flow cytometry for CD56/CD16/CD9/CD103/KIR as the sole endpoint; Cerdeira 2013 is 7 d at 1% vs 21% O2 with the same class of endpoint. Neither contains an in vivo arm, a congenic/genotype marker, a barcode, or live imaging. No labelled human blood NK cell has ever been shown to enter decidua. INF_INVITRO is correct and INF_MARKER/INF_KINETIC are correctly listed alongside. No INF_TRAJECTORY is present (G2 not engaged). (2) NO GENUINE FATE-MAPPING WAS MISSED FOR THE CLAIM AS STATED. The mouse in vivo work (Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026 PMID 42417504; Tatematsu/Sojka Mucosal Immunol 2025 PMID 39708955) concerns mouse splenic cNK -> CD49a+Eomes+ uterine trNK, i.e. registry claim T2, a different species and a different endpoint marker set; importing it into T3 would double-count. (3) THE AUDITOR'S `controls` FIELD IS FACTUALLY WRONG AND MUST BE CORRECTED. It asserts "ABSENT AND DECISIVE: no proliferation/division tracking (no CFSE, no Ki67, no cell counts per gate) ... no rigorous quantification of post-sort CD16- contamination in the critical CD16+ sorted arm". All three assertions are contradicted by the paper, including by the auditor's OWN archive file at /home/user/aaa/refs/T3_PMC1805591_FULLTEXT.txt line 98, which I re-read, and by my independent PMC fetch. Keskin Results state verbatim: "CD16+ pNK cells were sorted to very high purity (i.e., the contamination with CD16- pNK cells was <0.1%) (Fig. 5C), making it highly improbable that these results were caused by selective outgrowth of small numbers of contaminating cells of the other subset during the 2-week incubation. This transition of phenotype was accompanied by cell division, although not at levels sufficient to suggest outgrowth of very rare cells. After CFSE labeling of sorted cells, both CD16+ and CD16- pNK cells proliferated under these conditions (although proliferation appeared to be lesser in the presence of TGFbeta1) (SI Fig. 7)." And: "cultures supplemented with TGFbeta1 did not display substantially larger numbers of dead or apoptotic cells compared with medium alone (SI Table 2) ... fewer cells were recovered from TGFbeta1 cultures". So CFSE division tracking WAS done, post-sort contamination WAS quantified at <0.1%, and apoptosis plus recovered-cell counts WERE reported. The paper explicitly raised and argued against the selective-outgrowth alternative. CONSEQUENCE: the auditor's `strongest_alternative_explanation` claim that "the assay is formally incapable of distinguishing conversion from selective outgrowth" is overstated and must be softened. The defensible statement is weaker: Keskin addressed selection with CFSE + <0.1% purity + viability/recovery counts, but the CFSE data are a qualitative SI figure with no proliferation-index or absolute per-gate accounting, the sorted-arm panels are labelled "representative" with no stated n, and TGF-beta1 REDUCED proliferation (which argues against outgrowth but also means the CFSE arm was never used to model the gate shift quantitatively). Selection is argued against, not quantitatively excluded. NET: the class is INF_INVITRO for the right reason - a population-level flow readout on an in vitro culture is not an in vivo lineage observation, no matter how well the selection artefact is controlled - not for the auditor's stated (and false) reason. The auditor's n/n_unit handling (16 independent experiments, 12/16, P=0.002 paired t test; donor counts never stated) I verified verbatim in the text and it is correct and G5-compliant.
adv.new_counter_evidence: TWO MAJOR ITEMS THE AUDITOR MISSED, BOTH IN VIVO, AND THEY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. (1) SOJKA DK, PLOUGASTEL-DOUGLAS B, YANG L, et al., eLife 2014;3:e01659, PMID 24714492, PMC3975579 - the canonical TWO-INDEPENDENT-LINEAGES paper, cited nowhere in the audited row. I pulled it (STATUS=OA_FULLTEXT, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T3_PMC3975579.txt) and read the results/methods directly from PMC. Methods: parabiosis of C57BL/6NCr (CD45.2) with B6-LY5.1/Cr (CD45.1) female mice, analysed day 14, "performed two independent times with four parabiosed animals in each experiment (total of 8 pairs)". Result: in uterus and skin, host CD49a+DX5- trNK were found essentially only in the host tissue, while CD49a-DX5+ cNK of both allotypes were found in both parabionts and the spleen reached near-complete chimerism - i.e. the uterine trNK compartment was NOT replenished from the circulation over 14 days. Genetic arms: Nfil3-/- mice LACK cNK but RETAIN uterine trNK; Tbx21-/- mice lack liver and skin trNK but RETAIN uterine trNK; uterine trNK are CD127-negative and present in athymic Foxn1-/- mice. Authors' conclusion verbatim: "there are at least four lineages of NK cells: cNK cells circulating in spleen, blood and other organs, thymic, and two trNK cell lineages - liver (and skin), and uterine." This is parabiosis + OBS_GENETIC support for the pre-existing-independent-lineage alternative and it directly opposes a recruitment/conversion model for uterine NK. (2) TATEMATSU BK & SOJKA DK, Mucosal Immunol 2025;18(2):390-401, PMID 39708955, doi 10.1016/j.mucimm.2024.12.009 - also cited nowhere in the audited row, and it is the paper Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026 itself relies on for parabiosis. Abstract: parabiosed mice + intravascular fluorescent antibody labelling + flow cytometry; C57BL/6J ovariectomised at 3 wk lacked uterine trNK entirely unless progesterone was administered; "Our parabiosis studies confirmed that the progesterone-responsive trNK cells are derived from peripheral cNK cells"; MPA-induced expansion of cNK-derived trNK was abolished by a progesterone-receptor antagonist. METHODS NOT READ - WebFetch of sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1933021924001326 and mucosalimmunology.org/article/S1933-0219(24)00132-6/fulltext both returned HTTP 403, no PMC deposit; recorded from abstract only per G3, and NOT graded as verified OBS. (3) THE DECISIVE POINT THE AUDITOR HAD NO WAY TO SEE WITHOUT (1) AND (2): these are the SAME senior author reversing herself. Sojka 2014 = uterine trNK are host-restricted at day-14 parabiosis and NFIL3-independent, therefore a distinct lineage from cNK. Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 = uterine trNK are derived from peripheral cNK, by parabiosis. Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026 (which I re-read via WebFetch of elifesciences.org/articles/109878) now states its position as trNK "arise from precursors in the cNK cell lineage" and frames the result as "plastic reprogramming of peripheral cNK cells upon entry into the gravid uterus" - abandoning the 2014 four-lineage model without a reconciling experiment. What changed between the two parabiosis results is duration and hormonal state, not a new lineage assay. That is a direct warning about how much weight any single chimerism read-out can carry, and it applies with full force to the human uterus-transplant/HSCT chimerism data the audited row leans on (Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461; Strunz/Ivarsson Sci Transl Med 2026 PMID 41811987 - I confirmed both PMIDs and titles are real via eutils esummary, but did NOT read either methods section; science.org paywall, so abstract-level only). (4) TWO WEAKNESSES IN THE MOUSE "FOR" EVIDENCE THE AUDITOR OVERSTATED. From my own WebFetch of the eLife text: Barahona 2026 gives NO numeric conversion percentage anywhere in Results or Methods - Fig 1D shows "proportion of uterine ILC subsets derived from adoptively transferred splenic cNK cells" but the fraction of donor cells that actually converted is never stated; and the conditional-knockout arm is interpreted by the authors themselves as "a defect in tissue RETENTION rather than recruitment", which is compatible with failure to retain an already-recruited population rather than failure to convert. Transfer n=4 dams (2.5x10^6 CD45.2+ splenic cNK, gd0.5 -> gd10.5); rescue arm n=3 reconstituted dams (3.0x10^6 CD45.1+); CKO n=5 dams/15 implantation sites vs n=6 littermates/54 sites at gd6.5. (5) I CONFIRM the auditor's local-precursor counter-evidence (Vacca 2011 PMID 21248224; Male 2010 PMID 20802153; Keskin's own Fig 6 decidual Lin-CD34+CD45+ HPC in 3/4 experiments) and add Keskin's own admission that this arm is contamination-vulnerable: "it cannot be eliminated that rare functional progenitors may have resulted from contamination with blood or with fetal HPC." (6) NOT_SEARCHED / NOT FOUND, stated per G3: I searched for a direct failed replication of Keskin's sorted-CD16+ conversion and found none - NONE for that specific search, not evidence of absence. I searched for clonal/barcode/somatic-variant lineage tracing of human pbNK into decidua and found NONE. I did NOT search the rhesus/non-human-primate decidual NK literature beyond one incidental hit (PMID 21900681) - NOT_SEARCHED.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings: G4 VIOLATION IN THE AUDITED ROW: all 21 searches it lists are NK/decidua-internal. It ran ZERO searches in the TRM, ILC or myeloid literature on the same process (circulating cell -> tissue-resident cell; TGF-beta-driven residency programming). I ran them; findings below, each from a paper I located and whose abstract/methods I read. (A) MYELOID - THE STRONGEST PRIOR AGAINST READING KESKIN AS ONTOGENY. Yona S et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23273845 ("Fate mapping reveals origins and dynamics of monocytes and tissue macrophages under homeostasis") and Hashimoto D et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23601688 ("Tissue-resident macrophages self-maintain locally throughout adult life with minimal contribution from circulating monocytes"), with Guilliams M et al. 2013, PMID 24043763 (alveolar macrophages from fetal monocytes). For roughly forty years "blood monocyte becomes tissue macrophage" was textbook, and it rested on EXACTLY the evidence class Keskin supplies: a circulating cell cultured in tissue-conditioned medium acquires the tissue cell's markers, plus phenotypic similarity between the blood cell and the tissue cell. Genuine fate mapping (Cx3cr1-CreER, Flt3-Cre, parabiosis) overturned it - most tissue macrophages are embryonically seeded and locally self-renewing. The in vitro differentiation assay was reproducible and was a correct statement about what the cell CAN do; it was a false statement about what the cell DOES do in vivo. That is precisely the inferential gap between Keskin's culture and claim T3, and it is the reason INF_INVITRO must not drift upward. The same field also supplies the anti-overgeneralisation control: Bain CC et al., Nat Immunol 2014, PMID 25151491, shows intestinal macrophages ARE constantly monocyte-replenished - so the answer is organ-specific and a mouse-uterus result cannot be exported to human decidua. (B) TRM - THE MARKERS KESKIN SCORES ARE A GENERIC TGF-BETA RESIDENCY PROGRAM. Mackay LK et al., Nat Immunol 2013, PMID 24162776 ("The developmental pathway for CD103+CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells of skin") and Zhang N & Bevan MJ, Immunity 2013, PMID 24076049 ("TGF-beta signaling controls the formation and maintenance of gut-resident memory T cells by regulating migration and retention"). TGF-beta-driven induction of CD103 (alphaE integrin) on a circulating lymphocyte entering any tissue is the canonical, organ-nonspecific residency program - the same cytokine and the same integrin Keskin reports, in a completely different lineage and a completely different organ. This independently confirms the audited row's second alternative (CD9/CD103/CD49a = generic TGF-beta imprint, not decidual identity) and matches Keskin's own Discussion concession that "the changes observed may not be specific to the decidual tissue but may occur when NK cells enter any tissue expressing TGFbeta". Zhang & Bevan's title carries the sharper methodological lesson: TGF-beta controls MIGRATION AND RETENTION. Therefore a TGF-beta-dependent change in the number of resident-phenotype cells is NOT evidence of conversion, because retention and conversion are confounded by the same signal. This directly undercuts the Barahona 2026 Tgfbr2-Ncr1-iCre arm, whose own authors concede "a defect in tissue retention rather than recruitment" - the knockout phenotype is exactly what a pure retention defect predicts, with no conversion step required. (C) TRM CLONALITY - THE EXPERIMENT THE dNK FIELD HAS NEVER RUN. Gaide O et al., Nat Med 2015;21:647-653, PMID 25962122 ("Common clonal origin of central and resident memory T cells following skin immunization"): high-throughput sequencing of TCRbeta CDR3 tracked thousands of unique clones at once, and for every abundant skin TRM clone an identical-TCR TCM clone was present in the lymph node. That is how the T cell field promoted "circulating becomes resident" from marker similarity to a clonal statement. NK cells have no rearranged receptor, so this exact trick is unavailable - but the equivalents exist and none has been applied to human pbNK -> dNK: KIR/HLA allotype tracking, mtDNA or somatic-SNP single-cell lineage tracing, or transposon/LARRY barcoding. This is the concrete missing experiment for T3, and its absence is why the claim cannot rise above INF_INVITRO. (D) ILC - THE MOST DIRECTLY TRANSFERABLE RESULT, AND IT FAVOURS LOCAL MAINTENANCE. Gasteiger G, Fan X, Dikiy S, Lee SY, Rudensky AY, Science 2015;350(6263):981-985, PMID 26472762 ("Tissue residency of innate lymphoid cells in lymphoid and nonlymphoid organs"): by parabiosis, ILCs in adult mice are tissue-resident cells "maintained and expanded locally" under physiologic conditions, under systemic perturbation of immune homeostasis, AND during acute helminth infection; only at LATE timepoints after infection did "cells from hematogenous sources help to partially replenish the pool of resident ILCs". Applied to T3: for the ILC family the default is local self-renewal, with blood-derived replenishment a slow, perturbation-dependent, PARTIAL minority contribution. The massive dNK expansion of early pregnancy is therefore more parsimoniously explained by local proliferation of a resident or local-precursor pool than by mass conversion of mature pbNK. Note that this same paper cites Sojka 2014 - and its "late timepoints only, partial" finding predicts the Sojka-2014-versus-Tatematsu-2025 discrepancy exactly: short parabiosis reads out residency, long and hormone-driven parabiosis reads out replenishment. Neither reading licenses "mature pbNK converts to dNK". (E) SHARED METHODOLOGICAL CONTROL THE HUMAN WORK LACKS. Anderson KG, Mayer-Barber K, Sung H, et al., Nat Protoc 2014;9:209-222, PMID 24385150 ("Intravascular staining for discrimination of vascular and tissue leukocytes") - the field-standard control against scoring a cell sitting in the tissue vasculature as tissue-resident. Barahona 2026 used it (3 ug anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 i.v., 3 min before euthanasia) and Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 used it. NO human study bearing on pbNK -> dNK has any equivalent, and human first-trimester decidua from elective terminations is blood-contaminated by construction - the same confound Keskin concedes for his decidual CD34+ arm. Any future human chimerism claim (uterus transplant, HSCT) that lacks an intravascular-labelling or equivalent perfusion control should be discounted on this basis.

adv.load_bearing_reason: MEDIUM is correct; I considered both HIGH and LOW and rejected both. CONCRETE NAMED DOWNSTREAM DEPENDENCY, INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: Kopcow HD / Cerdeira AS et al., "Induced Human Decidual NK-Like Cells Improve Utero-Placental Perfusion in Mice", PLoS One 2016;11(10):e0164353, PMID 27736914 - confirmed real by eutils esummary (2016, PLoS One, exact title match) and independently surfaced by my own lit.py search, not merely inherited from the audited row. This paper manufactures "idNK" cells using precisely the Cerdeira hypoxia + TGF-beta1 + 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine protocol and infuses them into pregnant mice as a proposed preeclampsia cell therapy. Its entire premise is that the in vitro product IS a decidual NK cell. If the endpoint is a generic TGF-beta/hypoxia residency imprint rather than decidual identity - which the G4 TRM literature (Mackay PMID 24162776; Zhang & Bevan PMID 24076049) makes the more parsimonious reading, and which Keskin's own Discussion concedes - then the therapeutic rationale, not just the nomenclature, is undermined. SECOND AND THIRD DEPENDENCIES, VERIFIED IN THE REGISTRY: I read /home/user/aaa/phaseA/claims.json directly. X3 ("Tumour NK -> decidual-like / pro-angiogenic phenotype", initial "INFERENCE (phenotypic similarity)") and T5 ("Glycodelin-A -> dNK-like phenotype", initial "IN VITRO") both exist with exactly the gradings the audited row quoted, and both inherit their operational definition of the "dNK-like" endpoint (CD16-/CD9+/CD49a+/KIR+/VEGF-secreting/hypocytotoxic) from the Keskin-Cerdeira induction protocol. Degrading T3's endpoint specificity forces both to be re-read as INF_MARKER on a non-specific marker set. WHY NOT HIGH: T3 carries no weight for the core developmental claims (D1-D4) or for the best-evidenced peripheral claim (P1), and - this is the change from the audited row's reasoning - the mouse in vivo uterine claim T2 does NOT depend on T3 at all. T2 now rests on Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955, parabiosis + intravascular labelling) and Barahona/Yokoyama 2026 (PMID 42417504, congenic transfer + Tgfbr2 conditional knockout), both of which stand or fall on their own mouse evidence. So T3's collapse would not propagate to T2, which caps the blast radius. WHY NOT LOW: a live translational program (PMID 27736914) and two registry claims' measurement endpoints are downstream, and the audited row is right that T2's mouse transfer result is routinely read back onto T3 in the secondary literature as if it validated the human claim - a cross-species leak this audit blocks. One correction to the audited row's load-bearing text: it asserts T2's mouse result is "routinely read back onto T3"; that is the right worry, but the row should also record the reverse hazard I found - the Yokoyama/Sojka lab's own position on uterine trNK origin has reversed between 2014 (PMID 24714492, four distinct lineages, uterine trNK NFIL3-independent and host-restricted in parabiosis) and 2025-2026 (cNK-derived), with no reconciling experiment published. Any downstream claim that cites the mouse literature as settled on uterine NK origin is citing a field that has changed its answer once already.
